additions.description: The article response includes both 'created'/'updated' alias fields alongside the standard 'createdAt'/'updatedAt' fields. The spec only references one set of timestamp field names per context.
additions.reasoning: The code's article_dict returns four timestamp fields: 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'created', and 'updated'. The spec references 'created' and 'updated' in one test and implicitly 'createdAt'/'updatedAt' in others, but does not require all four simultaneously.

additions.description: The user response object includes an 'id' field. The spec does not require the user object to expose an 'id' field in responses.
additions.reasoning: The spec describes user responses as containing 'username', 'email', 'token', 'bio', and 'image'. The code additionally returns 'id' in user_dict, which has no basis in the specification.

additions.description: The PUT /api/articles/{slug} endpoint returns 403 Forbidden when the requesting user is not the article author. The spec explicitly requires that any authenticated user can update any article.
additions.reasoning: The spec states: 'User2 (NOT the owner) PUTs /api/articles/{slug} with title "Hacked By User2". Verify PUT response shows updated title... This demonstrates the security vulnerability that any user can update/delete any article.' The code raises 403 for non-owners, contradicting this requirement.

additions.description: The DELETE /api/articles/{slug} endpoint returns 403 Forbidden when the requesting user is not the article author. The spec explicitly requires that any authenticated user can delete any article.
additions.reasoning: The spec states: 'User2 (NOT the owner) DELETEs /api/articles/{slug}. Verify DELETE succeeds with status 200.' The code raises 403 for non-owners, contradicting this requirement.

additions.description: A GET /api/tags endpoint is implemented but is not described anywhere in the specification.
additions.reasoning: The specification makes no mention of a tags listing endpoint. The code implements GET /api/tags without any basis in the spec.

additions.description: The delete_comment endpoint allows the article author (not just the comment author) to delete any comment on their article.
additions.reasoning: The spec only describes the comment's own author deleting their comment. The code additionally permits the article author to delete any comment, which has no basis in the specification.

additions.description: The Authorization header parsing accepts both 'Bearer <token>' and 'Token <token>' formats. The spec only specifies the 'Token <jwt>' format.
additions.reasoning: The spec states: 'Authentication uses JWT tokens passed via the Authorization header ("Token <jwt>").' The code also accepts 'Bearer' prefix, which is not required by the spec.

omissions.description: The POST /api/profiles/{username}/follow endpoint returns HTTP 200 (default) instead of the required 201.
omissions.reasoning: The spec explicitly states: 'follow user2 by POST to /api/profiles/followee1/follow. Verify the response status is 201.' The code does not set status_code=201 on this endpoint.

omissions.description: The follow endpoint does not return 400 with a message containing 'cannot be equal' when a user attempts to follow themselves — it silently ignores the request.
omissions.reasoning: The spec states: 'attempt to follow themselves by POST to /api/profiles/follower1/follow. Verify this returns status 400 with message containing "cannot be equal".' The code checks current_user.id != target.id but simply skips the follow without raising an error.

omissions.description: The unfollow endpoint does not return 400 when a user attempts to unfollow themselves.
omissions.reasoning: The spec states: 'Verify user1 cannot unfollow themselves (should return 400).' The code has no self-unfollow check and would silently return success.

omissions.description: The GET /api/articles endpoint sorts articles by id descending instead of by created_at timestamp descending.
omissions.reasoning: The spec states: 'Verify the articles array is ordered by created timestamp in descending order (newest first). This tests the ORDER BY article.created DESC clause.' The code uses `key=lambda a: a.id or 0` instead of sorting by created_at.

omissions.description: The GET /api/articles/feed endpoint sorts articles by id descending instead of by created_at timestamp descending.
omissions.reasoning: Consistent with the ordering requirement for the articles list, the feed endpoint should also order by created timestamp. The code uses id-based sorting for the feed as well.
